key_insight: Linking fracture-tip sampling distance to mesh resolution enables convergent stress intensity factor estimates where conventional nearest-tip sampling fails.
engineering_relevance: More reliable stress intensity factors support accurate decisions about whether a pre-existing fracture will propagate.
method: Extract stress intensity factors using two-point displacement correlation.
Balance asymptotic truncation error against numerical discretization error to derive a sampling-distance scaling law.
Validate with standard quadratic finite elements, quarter-point quadratic finite elements, and a multi-point stress approximation finite volume method.
evidence_signal: On pure-mode and mixed-mode fracture benchmarks, scaling-based sampling produced decreasing errors under mesh refinement across all three discretization methods, unlike nearest-tip sampling.
watch_item: The abstract provides no explicit scaling formula or error rates, so implementation requires consulting the full paper.
paper_title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
